conductivity.location: Section 2.4, Table 2.4.1 and data-set summary [16], printed page 70

comparison.note: The two NIST reviews disagree on the annealing temperature for this rod. IR 84-3007 reports 700 K and Monograph 177 Table 7.8 reports 973 K. The example RRR 100 in the existing thermal coupon is a parameter choice without a matched stock specimen.

heat_capacity.unit: J/(kg K) after molar mass conversion

comparison.kind: Three adiabatic calorimeters on high-purity copper
comparison.note: Range is from the abstract. Exact grade, anneal and measurement uncertainty need full-text verification.

condition_cross_check.condition: Cast OFHC ingot, cold rolled and then annealed at 400 °C for one hour, 15 µm mean grain diameter
condition_cross_check.note: The paper uses literature heat capacities for copper and measures heat content for brass. It does not verify total heat capacity for this annealed OFHC specimen.

deformation.method: Compression and free-end torsion with constant-rate and sequential tests
deformation.unit: True stress in MPa and dimensionless true strain
deformation.note: Bounds span the experiment program and do not imply every temperature-rate combination was tested. Use Figures 12–14 for compression cross-checks at 25, 269 and 541 °C.

deformation.condition: Oxygen-free rod and a separate electrolytic grade, vacuum annealed at 750 °C for seven hours
deformation.unit: Flow stress in MPa and dimensionless true strain
deformation.note: Dynamic recrystallization changes flow stress with accumulated strain. Keep the oxygen-free specimen distinct from the electrolytic grade.

reuse: NIST reuse guidance: https://www.nist.gov/open/license. This file records source citations and experimental metadata. Publisher reuse terms for full curves and raw measurements remain to be verified.
calibration_gaps: No same-stock, high-temperature heat capacity and deformation datasets have been verified. Retain the elemental thermal coupon independently of the stock-specific material.
Retrieve specimen compositions, uncertainty and eligible compression curves before calibrating a flow model. Test dynamic recrystallization and history-dependent recovery independently.
Cooling is a thermal boundary problem. The steel transformation and hardening model has no evidentiary basis for this oxygen-free copper.
Retain this material outside the playable catalog pending coverage under issue 96.
